key_insight: Exact or sufficiently accurate fermionic quantum error correction cannot be done with only free-fermion (Gaussian) operations; non-Gaussian resources are fundamentally required.
engineering_relevance: Any scalable fermionic quantum computing platform, including Majorana- and cold-atom-based systems, must budget for non-Gaussian gate overhead in both code preparation and error correction.
method: Proved that the logical space of any non-trivial fermionic error-correcting code contains no pure Gaussian state.
Used the incompatibility between fermionic error correction and Wick’s theorem to rule out free-fermion-only protection.
Derived a lower bound showing bounded-weight non-Gaussian gates for codeword preparation grow at least linearly with code distance and encoded modes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytic no-go theorems and lower bounds, plus a separate analysis showing Gaussian operations are limited for fermionic entanglement distillation.
watch_item: The results imply that implementing practical fermionic codes will require non-Gaussian operations, which may be costly and difficult to realize experimentally.
paper_title: Fermionic quantum error correction is never free
